title: Misrepresentation and induced assent
summary: Misrepresentation concerns a false or misleading representation that affects a party’s decision to agree. Analyze what was represented, why it was misleading, how it induced assent, and whether reliance was justified under the applicable rule.
notes:
A statement can be misleading through what it says, what it implies, or an omission that makes a partial account deceptive. Swinton and Kannavos distinguish mere silence in the circumstances presented from statements that create a false impression unless completed. Speakers of Sport separates predictions or promotional confidence from actionable factual commitments, while Vokes examines flattering opinions given by a party with superior knowledge to an inexperienced customer.

Contract avoidance for misrepresentation, damages in tort for fraud, and breach of an express warranty are related but distinct routes. Psenicska adds the problem of a specific no-reliance clause and what the plaintiffs agreed they were not relying on. A general merger clause and a specific disclaimer of reliance need not have the same effect. Preserve the jurisdiction, procedural stage, and precise representation before drawing a result.

topics.misrepresentation: The inquiry concerns how information affected agreement.
topics.assent: An apparent agreement may have been induced by a misleading representation.
